ir.note: Third-party IR control is supported since DSP firmware 30 (RME, 'Firmware Update ADI-2 DAC 26 / 30 - Remote it!'). The supplied RME Multi-Remote must be on code table 1 (green SEL LED) — the same table these codes belong to — and the unit's SETUP › Options › Remap Keys/Diagnosis › Remap Keys must be ON or Remote (ADI-2 DAC FS manual v3.4, ch. 9). Power On / Power Off are discrete, which is what an automation needs; Mute is a toggle (the manual: 'Mute the audio output'), there is no separate mute-off. The ADI-2 Pro family uses a different command table (e.g. Power On 0xA0 in a community LIRC file), so these codes are for the ADI-2 DAC / DAC FS only. Two-way volume sync as rooADI does it needs RME's USB MIDI protocol (adi2_protocol.zip) — a transport Lyr Link does not have yet.

metadata.notes: Codes come from RME's own IR command list (quoted on the RME forum: power on 0x20, power off 0x14, volume down 0x21, volume up 0x22, coaxial 0x23, optical 0x24, USB 0x25, mute 0x2A) and agree byte for byte with a decoded Global Caché capture of the real remote (decoded 2026-10-03; the capture's Power On line has one extra pulse and was not used). Not yet sent from a Lyr Bridge to a real unit. Bass/treble/balance/EQ codes exist in RME's list but were not transcribed here because only the eight above could be confirmed from two sources.

encoding.note: Extended NEC. RME call the address "1234": the frame carries byte 0x12 then 0x34, and Lyr's encoder sends the low byte first, so the 16-bit address is 0x3412.

controls.note: Source detail: RME ADI-2 DAC IR command list (https://archiv.rme-audio.de/download/adi2dac_ir_commands.zip) as quoted on the RME forum (https://forum.rme-audio.de/viewtopic.php?id=28980); cross-checked by decoding a published Global Caché capture (https://justpaste.it/76oxh) to the same address and command bytes
